text: Kitzingen (German: [ˈkɪt͡sɪŋən] ()) is a town in Bavaria, capital of Kitzingen. It is part of the Franconia geographical region and has around 21,000 residents. Surrounded by vineyards, Kitzingen County is the largest wine producer in Bavaria. It is said to be Franconia's wine trade center.
title: Kitzingen

text: Marcus Nathan Bent (born 19 May 1978) is a retired English professional footballer. A former England under-21 international, he played 573 games and scored 113 goals for fourteen different clubs.
title: Marcus Bent

author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
text: Zdeněk Hoření (9 February 1930 – 12 February 2021) was a Czechoslovak journalist and politician. He was Editor-in-Chief of Rudé právo. He was a member of the Communist Party. He was born in Frýdštejn, First Czechoslovak Republic. From 1986 to 1990, he was a member of the Federal Assembly. Before, he was a member of the Czech National Council from 1976 to 1986. Hoření died of COVID-19 during the COVID-19 pandemic in the Czech Republic in Prague on 12 February 2021 at the age of 91, three days after his birthday.
title: Zdeněk Hoření

text: "Gi' Me Wings" is a 1981 song by Rod Stewart. It is the fifth and final single from his tenth studio album Foolish Behaviour (1980). It was released only as a single in Japan and went to number 45 on the Billboard Mainstream Rock chart.
title: Gi' Me Wings

author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
text: cowsay is a configurable text filter that generates an ASCII art image of a cow (or other creatures) saying or thinking a message. Originally created by Tony Monroe in 1999, the program is written in Perl and has become a light-hearted tool often found in terminal screenshots, IRC, and documentation. Besides the default cow, users can choose from a wide variety of alternative character templates (called ".cow" files), including Tux the Penguin and various fantasy animals. A companion program, cowthink, renders messages as thoughts (using thought bubbles instead of speech bubbles). The cow’s expression and behavior can be customized using parameters that alter its eyes, tongue, or replace it entirely. Cowsay has achieved cult status in hacker culture and continues to be included in many Linux distributions. It was even featured as Debian’s “Package of the Day” in 2007.
title: Cowsay
